prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” roofer for everyone — the right company depends on your exact needs (roof type, budget, property, insurance, timing). Instead of naming one firm I can’t verify in real time, here’s how to find the best Miami contractor for a hurricane‑rated roof replacement and what to require from them.

What to look for
- Miami‑Dade County NOA and Florida Building Code compliance: they must install products/systems that meet Miami‑Dade or FBC wind/impact requirements. Ask for the NOA (Notice of Acceptance) number or documentation for the exact roof system and materials they’ll use.  
- Proper licensing and insurance: check the contractor’s Florida license (search Florida DBPR) and confirm general liability and workers’ comp insurance.  
- Manufacturer certifications: GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Platinum Preferred, or similar show manufacturer training and warranties.  
- Proven hurricane systems: standing‑seam metal, properly installed concrete/terracotta tile with hurricane straps, or high‑wind/impact‑rated shingles (Class 4) are common choices. Ask which system they recommend for your structure and wind zone.  
- Local experience: ask for recent Miami/Dade roof replacements done to hurricane standard, with references and photos (preferably within last 2–3 years).  
- Written performance warranty and workmanship warranty (not just material warranty).  
- Permit and inspection handling: they should obtain permits and work with inspectors/engineers if needed.  
- Insurance claim experience: if you plan to use insurance, a contractor experienced with claims and public adjusters is helpful — but beware of storm-chasing contractors.

Questions to ask any contractor
- “Can you show the NOA or FBC documentation for the exact product/system you will install?”  
- “Are you licensed in Florida? What’s your license number?” (verify on DBPR)  
- “Do you carry general liability and workers’ comp? Can I see certificates?”  
- “Do you have manufacturer certifications? Which ones?”  
- “Can you provide 3 recent local references and photos of completed hurricane‑rated roofs?”  
- “What warranties do you offer (materials and workmanship) and are they transferable?”  
- “Who will handle permits and inspections?”  
- “What is the payment schedule and do you require a lien waiver?”

Red flags
- High pressure to sign immediately, “storm chaser” tactics, very large upfront deposits, no local references, no license or insurance proof, salespeople who discourage you from getting multiple bids.

How to find candidates
- Search Google/Yelp/Angi and filter for contractors with many recent reviews in Miami (check review content).  
- Check BBB ratings and complaints.  
- Verify license at Florida DBPR and check Miami‑Dade County product approvals if they cite NOAs.  
- Ask neighbors, HOA, or local roofing suppliers for recommendations.

If you want, I can:
- Help vet specific company names you found (what to check or red flags).  
- Suggest likely high‑quality installers near your zip code if you give your Miami zip code (I can’t browse live, but I can tell you how to verify them quickly).

Tell me your zip code, roof type (tile/metal/asphalt), and whether you’ll use insurance — I’ll guide you toward the best next steps and what to ask specific contractors.
